title: Liberalised Remittance Scheme: Navigating RBI Curbs & Remittance Strategy
description: The Liberalised Remittance Scheme (LRS) allows resident Indians to send up to USD 250,000 abroad per financial year for various purposes. Recent market specul.

faq.q: What is the current annual limit under the Liberalised Remittance Scheme (LRS)?
faq.a: The current annual limit under the LRS is USD 250,000 (or its equivalent in other foreign currencies) per financial year for resident individuals. This limit applies to the aggregate of all remittances made by an individual.

faq.q: Is TCS on LRS remittances a final tax?
faq.a: No, Tax Collected at Source (TCS) on LRS remittances is not a final tax. It is an advance tax payment that can be claimed as a credit against your total income tax liability when you file your Income Tax Return (ITR). You may be eligible for a refund if the TCS collected exceeds your final tax liability.

faq.q: Can Non-Resident Indians (NRIs) use the LRS?
faq.a: No, the Liberalised Remittance Scheme (LRS) is exclusively for resident individuals. Non-Resident Indians (NRIs) are governed by different foreign exchange regulations for their remittances and investments.

faq.q: What are some common purposes for LRS remittances?
faq.a: Common purposes for LRS remittances include sending money for education abroad, medical treatment, gifts to relatives, family maintenance, travel expenses, and investments in foreign stocks, bonds, or property.

faq.q: How do I know if RBI has changed LRS rules?
faq.a: Any changes to the LRS rules would be officially announced by the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) through circulars and press releases on its official website. It is advisable to refer to these official sources for accurate and up-to-date information.

faq.q: Are all LRS transactions subject to TCS?
faq.a: TCS is applicable to LRS remittances exceeding ₹7 lakh in a financial year. The rate of TCS varies depending on the purpose of the remittance (e.g., education, medical, or other purposes). Remittances below ₹7 lakh are generally exempt from TCS.
